title: Resilient button interaction: transient-disabled recovery & contextual affordances
creator: Ava Morales
description: Goal: Reduce visible jumpiness and interaction loss when buttons enter a temporary disabled state (network backoff, rate-limit hold, policy gating) and provide clear, accessible affordances for icon-only and compact variants. Scope includes token updates for transient-disabled alpha/contrast, motion timing for recovery transitions, an accessible reason popover pattern, and a small compatibility shim to avoid regressions introduced in last theme pass.
acceptance_criteria: When a button becomes transiently disabled (server-driven or local debounce), its visual change must not cause layout shift or icon reflow for any size/variant.

Transient-disable must use standardized tokens: token names proposed (button.transientDisabled.background, button.transientDisabled.border, button.transientDisabled.text, button.transientDisabled.iconOpacity). These tokens map across light/dark/edge themes.

Recovery transition: when re-enabled within 250ms the button should animate opacity only (no layout repaint) with a maximum combined duration of 180ms; beyond 250ms show full re-enabled state with 220ms easing. Documented easing curves and CSS variables provided.
Icon-only buttons retain consistent hit target and ghost-outline during transient-disabled states; no icon re-scaling or center offset should occur.

Accessible reason: a lightweight tooltip/popover appears on focus or long-press explaining the temporary disable reason; it must be keyboard reachable, screen-reader announced, and dismissible. Pattern documented with ARIA attributes.
No regressions in existing button stories: all Primary/Secondary/Outline/Ghost/Icon stories pass visual diffing checks in Chromatic and internal snapshot tests.
Performance: CSS-only approach for visual transitions where possible; fallback JS only for browsers that lack CSS variable transition support (documented list).
updates: 2026-02-24 — Initial ticket created after discovery session: observed flicker in compact icon-button when server responds with 429 and UI toggles disabled state. Collected repro cases from QA (stack traces and video captures).
2026-02-27 — Quick ADR: prefer opacity-only transitions for recovery to avoid layout reflow. Shared draft token names with Tokens guild for mapping into alias layer.

2026-03-02 — Design review with PM (Liam Chen) and Eng (Priya Sinha). Agreed to prototype CSS approach and a small JS guard for older browsers. PM requests accessible reason copy variants for legal/regulatory flows.
2026-03-05 — Prototyped in storybook: compact icon-button no longer jumps; minor contrast issue found on high-contrast dark theme for outline variant (filed follow-up).
2026-03-10 — Received engineering estimate for implementation (ENG-52012) and synced on tokens mapping. UX copy for tooltip approved by legal; prepared acceptance criteria for QA.
decisions: Use dedicated transient tokens instead of reusing disabled tokens to allow separate motion rules and accessibility thresholds.
Prefer CSS variables + transition-timing for primary recovery path; include a 250ms debounce window to prevent flicker on brief disables.
Icon-only hit target must not change size; reveal a ghost-outline with maintained padding rather than shrinking icon or adding decorative elements.
Implement reason popover as an optional composable (not default) — product teams choose to surface it only for policy or billing reasons.
Avoid expensive layout properties (width/height/transform-scale) during transitions to keep 60FPS on low-power devices.
notes: Token proposals include accessible contrast targets (WCAG 2.1 AA) for transientDisabled.text when used on outline/ghost variants.
Edge-case: when multiple buttons in a row toggle disabled simultaneously (batch error), ensure staggered focus management to avoid focus loss; engineering to propose focus retention behaviour.
QA should test on Windows High Contrast theme, Safari iOS, and low-power mode Android to validate animation fallback path.
Related design debt: earlier theme pass introduced a border alias that inadvertently reduced icon-button contrast; addressed in separate ticket DES-120301 (linked internally).
